column1: # The five models the README's speed table always reports. One per line:
#   <label>  TAB  <name-or-path>  TAB  <-n>  TAB  <extra flags>
# **Five, fixed, and spanning the whole range Chaos claims to cover** — Atur's
# rule, 2026-08-31: one huge, two medium, one small, one fast. A speed table with
# a different set each time is a table nobody can compare against last month's.
#   v4flash    144.44 GiB   streams 3.22 GiB of experts per token from disk
#   qwen3moe    17.28 GiB   streams a little: routed experts, trunk resident
#   qwen3-4b     2.33 GiB   dense, fits with room to spare
#   falcon3      0.98 GiB   dense, small
#   qwen2        0.37 GiB   the ceiling case: nothing to stream, nothing to wait for
# `-n` differs per model on purpose. A short run on a fast model measures the
# load, not the generation; a long run on V4-Flash measures the same 2 s token
# forty times over and costs half an hour. Each is the smallest count whose
# three runs agreed within the machine's own drift when the harness was written.
# **`--force` on qwen3moe is not optional and not a wart**: `qwen3moe` is not in
# `VERIFIED_ARCHITECTURES` — its eight-prompt diff came back 1 FAIL — so the
# runner refuses it by name. It is in this table because it is the second
# streaming model on the machine, and the flag is here so the table is honest
# about which rows are verified architectures and which are not.
DeepSeek-V4-Flash
Qwen3-30B-A3B
Qwen3-4B
Falcon3-1B
Qwen2-0.5B
